rulings.model: The IRS instruction says to check column (c) if the person 'was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled.' For a person over 13 at year-end the restatement does not use the care-time disabled helper; it only requires the separate 2025 incapacity input, so it can check the box even if the disability did not exist when the care was provided.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; the model says that for a person over 13 at the end of 2025 the box can be checked "even if the disability did not exist when the care was provided". i2441 p. 3, Column (c): "Check the box in column (c) if the qualifying person listed in column (a) was over age 12 at the time the care was provided and was disabled". A person over 13 at year end was over 12 throughout 2025, and the expenses on line 2 are only those "for this person's care while they were a qualifying person (under age 13, or not able to care for themselves)" (dependent.dc_paid; p503 p. 3, "You determine a person's qualifying status each day"), so every included expense was for care while the person was over 12 and disabled. The box is right whenever the line has an entry.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.dc_line30 (owner ruling, Stage 15, T-048). The model reads the rejected reading (column (d) net of benefits). Its further claim that deductible benefits (line 24) can stay in the computation is a misreading: f2441.line30 subtracts f2441.line28, "Add lines 24 and 25", from the column (d) total, which is Form 2441 line 30, "Don't include in column (d) any benefits shown on line 28 above". The dc_paid help sentence "Form 2441 subtracts the benefits you exclude" names only excluded benefits, but nothing the filer enters depends on it (both kinds are included in the expenses asked), so no amount or answer changes.

rulings.model: The helper includes expenses paid with dependent care benefits, but Form 2441 line 2(d) says "If you completed Part III, don't include in column (d) any benefits shown on line 28." It also excludes only the parent of your child under 13, while the IRS excludes the parent of your qualifying child.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; two register readings. (1) amb.2025.dc_line30 (chosen reading: column (d) shows each person's expenses including those paid with dependent care benefits, and line 30 subtracts line 28 from the total; owner's decision, Stage 15 decision 6). Form 2441 line 30: "Complete line 2 on page 1 of this form. Don't include in column (d) any benefits shown on line 28 above. Then, add the amounts in column (d) and enter the total here"; the instructions give no rule for dividing line 28 among persons; the model reads the rejected reading. (2) The care-provider exclusion is amb.2025.dc_ineligible_providers: i2441 p. 2, item 4, "the parent of your qualifying child", against p503 p. 8, Payments to Relatives or Dependents, "The parent of your qualifying person if your qualifying person is your child and under age 13"; the project asks Pub. 503's list (owner's decision, Stage 15 decision 6), the more specific text, so the helper's "the parent of your child under 13" is the chosen reading, not a misstatement. Project stands.
